newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares close up on credit-easing talk.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares close up on credit-easing talk.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices closed sharply higher on Tuesday on a rebound after Monday's steep falls and also talk that Beijing plans to ease its credit controls later this year, brokers said.
The B share index rose 5.69 points or 4.17 percent to close at 142.15 on volume of 28.06 million shares worth HK$136 million compared with the previous session's HK$89 million.
The A share index rallied 13.92 points or 4.36 percent to end at 333.17, with turnover rising to 4.59 billion yuan from 3.78 billion yuan on Monday.
There was talk that China planned to ease its credit controls by lowering bank reserve requirements later this year, which boosted market sentiment, brokers said.

"The rumours fueled strong institutional demand for financial industry issues in the A share market and pushed the A share index sharply higher, with the B share market following suit," a broker said.
Shenzhen's A share market leader Shenzhen Development Bank was the most actively traded stock on volume of 32.72 million shares and advanced 1.13 yuan to 17.02 yuan.
Shaanxi International Trust and Investment closed at its 10 percent limit-up of 9.65 yuan on heavy trade of 26.05 million shares.
Xinjiang Hongyuan Trust soared 0.83 yuan or 9.95 percent to 9.17 yuan.

All 43 Shenzhen-listed B shares gained on Tuesday, with Health Mineral Water rising HK$0.43 to end at its 10 percent limit-up of HK$4.70 on volume of 923,185 shares, making it the day's best B share performer.
Television tube maker SEG surged HK$0.44 or 7.79 percent to HK$6.09, with 1.38 million shares traded.
Changan Automobile climbed HK$0.32 to HK$4.59 on the session's most active trade of 5.20 million shares on institutional buying, brokers said.
